title: Grammarly Pricing 2026: Free vs Pro vs Business Plans
summary: Grammarly pricing includes a free plan and paid Pro and Business tiers. Compare plans, features, and costs to pick the right option for your needs.
body_markdown:
## Fix repetitive draft checks with Activepieces


If your cost is the routine around your writing rather than the writing itself, Activepieces can take that routine off your hands.


It's an open source, MIT-licensed automation platform with 746 integrations that connects apps and runs steps for you, so your workflow steps run automatically.


Think of the person who spends part of every week collecting drafts, pasting them into a checker, chasing someone for sign-off, and typing the outcome into a tracking sheet.


Hours that never show up on any invoice are what doing nothing about that costs, and **no Grammarly plan, free or paid, touches them** .


Here's the flow it can run, in order:


1. A trigger fires when a new draft lands in a chosen[Google Drive](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/google-drive) folder.
2. An AI step reads the draft and reviews it against your written style guide.
3. The result goes to an approver in[Slack](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/slack) , the team chat app, so the person who signs off sees it where they already work.
4. When the approver says yes, the outcome is logged as a new row in a Google Sheet.


That sequence shows where the manual work lives: collecting, reviewing, routing and recording. Each of those is a handoff, and handoffs are what a workflow handles well.


You don't have to wire those four steps by hand, which means the platform handles the connections for you.


Describe the Drive-to-Slack-to-Sheets process in Activepieces' built-in chat and what comes back is a published flow in your account, the same artefact a builder would have assembled, sitting under the same RBAC and audit logs as every other flow.


Each draft that passes through it leaves a run trace you can read step by step, so after one test draft you can open the live flow in your account and see exactly what happened at each of the four steps.


MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


What to take from it is that the tool is built for the gaps between people and apps, not for the sentence you're typing.


### What a workflow can and cannot replace


It can't replace Grammarly's checking inside the editor. Grammarly flags a clumsy sentence or a tone problem as you write, in the document, before anyone else sees it.


Because an Activepieces flow runs only after a draft exists and sits in a folder, it works on finished drafts, not on the keystroke.


The AI step also checks only what your style guide spells out, so a vague guide gets vague reviews, and it carries a cost: a run is 1 credit however many steps it has, but an AI step on a fast model costs 2 credits and on a smart model 10.


What it can replace is the shuttling. If a team already pays for shared style control and still loses time moving drafts and approvals by hand, the flow closes that gap.


If you write alone and the free plan covers you, there's likely nothing here worth building. Start with the one handoff that annoys you most, and add the rest only if it earns its keep.
